messages:
maria: Noticing a latency bump on chat-lite routes after yesterday's kernel affinity tweak. p50 went up ~60% for some tails.
kevin: Confirmed in canary metrics. KV prefix hit rate dropped noticeably — from ~97% to ~90% in the 14:00–16:00 window.
anand: Any recent changes to canonicalization or serialization? We shipped the stable-serialize change for toolcall args last week.
maria: Yup. I ran a quick compare of cache keys and found that previously we collapsed tool args into a generic token; now serializer emits full arg arrays which are getting hashed into the key. Example: 
``
old: prefix|route:chat-lite|sig:aa11|tools:ANY
new: prefix|route:chat-lite|sig:aa11|tools:[{"name":"date","args":["2026-01-01"]}]
```
jess: That would explain fragmentation. Small difference in key -> miss -> no KV warmup -> higher kernel cold latency.
daniel: Also, kernel selector moved some traffic to the fp16 path for these routes. fp16 kernel has lower throughput at small batch sizes and thus worse p50 when batching efficiency collapses.
benchbot: perf-summary: route=chat-lite p50_before=18ms p50_after=29ms kv_hit_before=97% kv_hit_after=90% batching_util_before=0.92 batching_util_after=0.78
kevin: Two levers: reduce key entropy or populate cache. We can either revert the serializer change for tool args or alter key construction to ignore non-impactful args.
anand: We need correctness guardrails. Some functions depend on args (e.g., payment.amount). Proposal: introduce tool_call_meta.include_in_cachekey boolean, default false. If true, include a canonicalized minimal args fingerprint; if false, omit args entirely.
maria: Quick mitigation: I patched keyer to drop tool args and re-ran prefixbench. kv_hit rose to 95% and p50 back to ~20ms. Patch is non-invasive but not ideal long-term.
jess: Short-term plan: ship the patch to 10% canary ASAP. Medium-term: add include_in_cachekey flag + SDK change + docs. Long-term: create a canonical signature library for cache keys decoupled from wire serializer so refactors don't change keys.
kevin: Also we should add a 'prefix-warmup' job that replays representative tool arg permutations for 24–48h before full rollouts of serializer-like changes. That should blunt misses during deployment.
devon: Note about kernel selector: add telemetry for kernel_choice and fallback events. I saw a fallback to fp32 during the window which increases per-token cost and messes with batch thresholds. Log excerpt: 
``
[2026-08-16T14:02:11Z] route=chat-lite seq=9 kernel=fp16_v2 affinity=low batch_wait=7ms fallback=fp32_v1 reason=quant-mismatch
```
anand: Good catch. We should alert if kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5% per route.
jess: Tests: add an eval harness scenario that asserts cache hit rate stability across serializer changes (simulate many small permutations of tool args).
maria: Action items I'll take: open a canary PR with tool-args-stripped keyer + warmup job; start a design doc for include_in_cachekey flag.
kevin: I'll wire kernel-selector metrics to perf dashboard and add the fallback alert.
anand: I'll draft the canonical-signature library spec and list the semantic primitives we must include in keys.
devon: I'll add a one-off job to replay historical traffic shaped to tool-arg distributions for the next 24h.
jess: +1. Let's also coordinate with SDKs so include_in_cachekey can be toggled before we flip defaults.
maria: Thanks. I'll update #eng-runtime once the canary is live and tag folks.
